sentences.text: Nanotyrannus was a mid-sized tyrannosauroid.
A press release noted that this animal would have reached approximately 17 feet in length and weighed 1000 pounds.
It possessed forelimbs that were both absolutely and proportionally larger than those of its relatives.
The rest of its teeth were serrated and compressed side-to-side in a condition called ziphodonty, which is not seen in tyrannosaurids.
The genus Nanotyrannus was described by Bakker, Williams, and Currie in 1988.
The genus was named by Bakker, Currie, and Williams in 1988.
The type species of Nanotyrannus is Gorgosaurus lancensis.
The type species of Nanotyrannus is Nanotyrannus lancensis.
Two species are currently recognized: N. lancensis described by Gilmore in 1946 and N. lethaeus described by Zanno and Napoli in 2025.
Nanotyrannus lethaeus is a subdivision of the genus described by Zanno and Napoli in 2025.
Nanotyrannus fossils are primarily known from the Hell Creek Formation.
Nanotyrannus had longer legs than contemporary taxa, suggesting it was a pursuit predator.
Bakker suggests that Nanotyrannus hunted in packs due to its weight and build.
Teeth from multiple Nanotyrannus individuals have been found in herbivore bones.
Researchers concluded that the N. lancensis holotype belongs to a mature individual based on hyoid bone sampling.
The genus Nanotyrannus was named by Bakker et al. in 1988.
One phylogenetic hypothesis suggests Nanotyrannus has close relations to Appalachiosaurus and Dryptosaurus.

Nanotyrannus fossils date to the Late Cretaceous.
Nanotyrannus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 68 to 66 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage in what is now North America.
Nanotyrannus lived in western North America during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 67 million years ago.
Many researchers favor the identification of the holotype skull as a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex based on subsequent research indicating it belonged to an immature animal.

Nanotyrannus lancensis specimens are reported to have 15-16 teeth on the upper jaw and 16-18 on the lower jaw, while adult Tyrannosaurus rex has 11-12 upper and 12-14 lower teeth.
